extraFields.label: Health insurance premium
extraFields.help: What you pay each month for health insurance, including the amount taken from your paycheck for an employer plan or a Marketplace plan after any tax credit.

single.note: KFF 2025: average worker contribution for single coverage $1,440 a year (about $120 a month, 16% of the $9,325 premium); the 80-200 spread around it is our estimate, KFF gives no distribution in its summary.

suburban.note: KFF 2025: average worker contribution for family coverage $6,850 a year (about $570 a month); worker share is 23% at large firms vs 36% at small firms of the $26,993 premium, i.e. about $520-$810 a month, which this range covers.

youngpro.note: Between KFF 2025 single ($120 a month) and family ($570 a month) worker contributions; KFF summary has no employee-plus-spouse figure, so the range is an estimate.

localTips.title: Compare health plans at open enrollment
localTips.why: Employer and Marketplace plans change prices every year, and the default is often to roll over into the same plan.
tips: At open enrollment, compare the premium plus the deductible you realistically expect to pay, not the premium alone.
If you are both covered at work, check whether one family plan or two separate plans costs less.
If you buy on HealthCare.gov or a state Marketplace, update your income: you may qualify for a bigger tax credit.

pct.note: Assumed saving from switching plans at open enrollment; no national study of the typical saving found, estimate kept.
